subsystems.name: Nanopore sensor
subsystems.role: the transducer — a hole a few nanometres wide that a polymer threads through, one unit at a time.
parts: protein pore (e.g. alpha-haemolysin, MspA) or solid-state pore in silicon nitride or graphene
insulating membrane or chip surface holding the pore

subsystems.name: Capture and ratcheting
subsystems.role: gets a strand to the pore mouth and then moves it step by step rather than letting it shoot through.

subsystems.name: Sample preparation
subsystems.role: turns a soil, ice or brine sample into a clean polymer solution without assuming earthly biochemistry.
parts: chemistry that binds adaptors to unknown backbone chemistries

subsystems.name: Readout electronics
subsystems.role: applies the driving voltage and records the tiny current changes as each unit passes.
parts: application-specific integrated circuit with one channel per pore

subsystems.name: Decoding and autonomy
subsystems.role: turns raw current traces into sequences and decides what is worth keeping.
parts: adaptive sampling that rejects uninformative reads

subsystems.name: Flight enclosure
subsystems.role: keeps the chemistry alive through launch, vacuum, radiation and temperature swings.

buildSteps.title: Choose or engineer the pore
buildSteps.detail: Protein pores are tuned by directed evolution so that different chemical units produce distinguishable current blockades; solid-state pores are drilled by focused electron beams for robustness and for geometries a protein cannot provide.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the sensor array
buildSteps.detail: Pores are inserted into lipid membranes or droplet interfaces formed directly on top of a chip, so that each microwell holds one pore connected to one electronic channel.

buildSteps.title: Attach the motor and adaptors
buildSteps.detail: A processive enzyme is coupled to the strand so that the polymer is pulled through at a controlled rate; because unknown polymers may not accept standard ligation chemistry, this step is the hardest to generalise.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the sample
buildSteps.detail: Polymers are extracted, salts and small molecules removed, and the solution buffered so that the pore stays open — critical when the starting material is a few grams of Martian regolith or an ice-melt brine.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the instrument
buildSteps.detail: Sensor chip, fluidics, reagent packs and readout board are integrated into a low-mass, low-power package comparable to a handheld sequencer.

buildSteps.title: Train the decoder
buildSteps.detail: Known polymers of many lengths and chemistries are run to build signal models; candidate non-terrestrial alphabets are handled as unknown classes rather than forced into A, C, G and T.

buildSteps.title: Validate terrestrially
buildSteps.detail: The instrument is tested on extreme environments — permafrost, hypersaline lakes, deep-sea sediments — and exposed to simulated Martian and icy-moon conditions.

buildSteps.title: Fly and prove
buildSteps.detail: A flight unit would first run on orbit or on a small lander, with results compared against ground labs to show that reading works outside Earth's biosphere.

prerequisites.why: handheld devices already read DNA and RNA in the field and on the International Space Station, proving the sensing principle is spaceworthy.
inorganic pores survive conditions that destroy lipid bilayers, but making them with consistent sub-nanometre size is still laboratory work.
every motor protein in use evolved for earthly nucleic acids; without an equivalent for another backbone, strands cross the pore too fast to read.
spacecraft electronics exist, but combining very low current noise with radiation hardness in one small chip is not routine.
current basecallers are trained on four letters of one chemistry; a genuinely alien polymer would need unsupervised interpretation first.

pathway.milestone: field sequencing on Earth and in orbit, plus instrument concepts such as MIT's nanopore-based life-detection programme
pathway.unlocks: confidence that pore-based reading survives space conditions.

pathway.milestone: bench demonstration of single-unit discrimination in a non-canonical nucleic acid or synthetic sequence-defined polymer
pathway.unlocks: a credible claim that the method is not restricted to Earth biochemistry.

pathway.milestone: a self-contained prototype tested in Mars and ocean-world analogues, with autonomous sample prep
pathway.unlocks: readiness for a lander or plume-flyby payload.

pathway.milestone: an in-situ instrument on a planetary mission feeding sample-return triage
pathway.unlocks: the ability to say whether a sample contains information-bearing polymers before deciding what to bring home.
